scope: All 113 unique maintained official URLs referenced by Platform, premium-product, Forwarder and SOAR data, plus bounded current release, upgrade, compatibility, receiver, runtime and security claims.

sourceInventory.method: Each maintained URL was fetched directly. Official GitHub latest-release API responses compensated for transient release-page rendering errors. A fetched source was not treated as a verified claim.
sourceInventory.changedSource: The canonical Enterprise 10.6 upgrade page now exposes an explicit 10.6 supported-path heading and table.
unavailable: Selected historical docs.splunk.com 8.1 and 8.2 pages returned retrieval errors; their historical records were preserved and not reverified.
Some GitHub HTML release pages returned transient rendering errors; current release identifiers were confirmed through the official GitHub Releases API instead.

claimChecks.section: Upgrade paths to version 10.6; current-version table
claimChecks.qualification: The table establishes release-line edges only. It does not establish exact maintenance, OS, app, receiver, topology, Cloud rollout, entitlement, region or authorization scope.
claimChecks.followUp: Retain the 10.4 source for older graph segments and monitor the versioned 10.6 table without pinning discovery to this release.

claimChecks.section: Key points for upgrading to version 10.6; direct Universal Forwarder upgrade; TLS and Federated Search prerequisites
claimChecks.qualification: UF-specific upgrade evidence remains separate from Heavy Forwarder, receiver and topology evidence.
claimChecks.followUp: Continue using the UF source for UF steps even though the Enterprise/HF release-line edges now coincide.

claimChecks.section: Forwarder-to-indexer compatibility; direct and intermediate forwarding tiers
claimChecks.qualification: The current matrix has no 10.6 forwarder row. Upgrade support and 10.6 certification do not prove receiver compatibility.
claimChecks.followUp: Keep 10.6 Enterprise receiver selections Not established until an explicit row is published.

claimChecks.productVersionEnvironment: UF/HF directly communicating with Splunk Cloud Platform; outgoing intermediate tier when present
claimChecks.qualification: The table stops at forwarder 10.4.x. Its direct-tier scope does not certify an indirectly connected forwarder or a hybrid topology.
claimChecks.followUp: Keep 10.6 Cloud receiver selections Not established and preserve the omitted Cloud 10.4 pairing for forwarder 10.0.

claimChecks.section: Current Splunk Cloud Platform and Premium App versions
claimChecks.qualification: The 10.6 documentation path still lists Cloud 10.5, ES 8.6 and ITSI 5.0. The page path and release notes do not establish selected-stack rollout or authorization.
claimChecks.followUp: Continue discovery for an explicit current-pairing update.

claimChecks.qualification: Customer-managed Enterprise compatibility does not establish Cloud managed availability, entitlement, regional authorization or exact patch readiness.
claimChecks.followUp: Verify exact maintenance releases and separate KV Store prerequisites during implementation planning.

claimChecks.qualification: The overview still lists September 23 as the newest milestone. SaaS milestones are not Collector or instrumentation installation paths.
claimChecks.followUp: Monitor for an October release-note page and keep component versions independently discovered.

claimChecks.section: September 22 updated build 243; Python 3.9 end of support
claimChecks.qualification: Build 243 fixes the two build 232 issues. Python 3.13-compatible automation is required; Cloud milestones are not installation paths.
claimChecks.followUp: Preserve both build identifiers and continue discovery beyond 8.7.

claimChecks.qualification: 6.4.1.x uses the documented 8.5.0 and Python migration bridge; 7.0.x and higher can move directly. Privileged and Phantom conversion paths are separate.
claimChecks.followUp: Expand older target coverage only from exact versioned tables.

claimChecks.section: Splunk Security Advisories; first current row
claimChecks.productVersionEnvironment: Enterprise, Universal Forwarder, AWS add-on and MCP Server
claimChecks.qualification: SVD-2026-0901 is an advance notice for October 7, not a present vulnerability or fixed-version record.
claimChecks.followUp: Recheck the published advisory rows on October 7 and preserve component-specific applicability.

unverifiedOrDeferred: Historical 8.1/8.2 source bodies that were unavailable during this run

validationOutcomes.detail: scripts/sync-release-metadata.cjs --check passed on the reconciled source.
The browser runtime blocked file:// and local-loopback pages. Structural journey tests passed, but that is not a native-browser result.

validationOutcomes.check: First live publication route and WebMCP parity
validationOutcomes.detail: The live Platform route used the 10.6 source, but the Heavy Forwarder WebMCP source catalog still attached the older 10.4 upgrade page to the 10.4→10.6 step. Publication was not accepted as final; a target-specific Heavy Forwarder source record and regression assertion were added before republishing.
